approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs using accepted task-local scores. A bounded population supplies parents from high-scoring bands. It generates fresh candidates either by joining connected fragments from two parents or by applying local mutation walks to one parent; direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is already disabled. Stable canonical identity checks and duplicate rejection form a surplus pool. A Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity, and correlated posterior draws choose the evaluated batch. Accepted offspring update both the full prediction archive and the breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove connected-fragment crossover so that every proposal follows the existing single-parent mutation walk. Ordinary mutation continuation, saturation handling and correlated posterior allocation remain. No completed child of this current baseline is supplied; the parallel children change allocation residuals, while this child changes the generating route. An earlier crossover removal lost endpoint score under a Parent that still allowed direct aromatic exchanges. Reusing that isolated removal on the exchange-free Parent tests whether recombination still contributes after the generator composition changed. The registered prediction is a material score loss, with a complete contrary result also answering the component question.

observed_bottleneck: The unresolved behavior is n-62daf219c70a continuing to allocate generation effort to two-parent recombination after direct aromatic exchange was removed, without a complete current-profile contrast establishing the route's endpoint contribution. The actual Parent summary.json and run.log pairs are complete, with macro mean 0.5956696497334577 and population SD 0.02659287062806747. Its full indexed audit records 75961 multi-parent opportunities, 34334 crossover attempts, 29730 crossover pool entries and 1492 accepted crossover offspring. Those accepted offspring include 180 strict best-parent beats, 74 incumbent improvements and 722 later-used parents; the full panel has 629 parent beats and 258 incumbent gains. These adaptive ancestry cohorts show real use, not individual causal contributions, and crossover faces the better of two parents as its comparison hurdle. The older exact route removal n-1faebb978a01 on the exchange-containing count-posterior Parent n-559d25e9c9c7 confirmed zero crossover across 73389 exposed attempts and completed every task. Its paired macro loss was 0.02886320397735261, with seed changes -0.06135954646465791, -0.004451554345889952 and -0.020778511121509968, despite parent beats rising from 624 to 713 and incumbent gains from 241 to 286. This supports predicting a loss here but does not transfer that measured effect to a changed composition. The exchange removal n-c55c3d520a2c changed search histories and raised its historical mean by 0.021326; the same-code current baseline reproduces its trajectories without adding independent seed evidence or a matched historical effect estimate. The distinct continuation removal n-29d770e728a6 lost 0.019179888857869958 on the older Parent, so this crossover test must preserve the one/two/three-call mutation law. Lower local yield, narrower molecules or fewer invalid graphs do not establish that recombination is dispensable.
hypothesis: Remove two-parent connected-fragment crossover from fresh-pool production, routing every proposal through the inherited single-parent local-mutation walk while retaining the count-based posterior and correlated batch allocation.

finding_summary.headline: Removing crossover lowers the matched mean by 0.054937 despite more local improvements
finding_summary.insights: This complete isolated removal supports a positive contribution of connected-fragment crossover in the current exchange-free search composition. That conclusion concerns the whole adaptive rerouting experiment, including changed ancestors and proposal histories; it does not assign value to an individual fragment or recombinant. A simple diversity-collapse explanation is inadequate: typed emitted cores increase from 1,851 to 1,924 while generic cores decrease from 1,118 to 1,009, and every Child emission retains a ring. Mean molecular size increases even though the extreme size range narrows. Molecular evidence likewise shows rich annulated amide, amine and heterocyclic families, with high-scoring conventional alternatives and persistent reactive bonds, difficult geometry and unspecified stereochemistry. More local wins or more typed cores therefore cannot substitute for the complete endpoint comparison or establish chemical feasibility. Which useful arrangements crossover helps search reach, and how that benefit interacts with the retained posterior and mutation continuation, remain open.
finding_summary.results: Crossover disappears from every one of 73,611 breeding attempts, even though a distinct eligible partner was available each time. The Parent used crossover on 34,334 attempts and evaluated 1,492 crossover offspring. The retained one-parent walks, all seven ordinary mutation families, accepted feedback and correlated posterior selection continue to operate. All three seeds complete. Mean final score falls from 0.595670 to 0.540732, a paired loss of 0.054937 against the registered 0.002 material-loss threshold. Seed losses are 0.112917, 0.004694 and 0.047200. Twelve of fifteen task-seed endpoints fall; median_2 and sitagliptin_mpo improve on seed 1, and zaleplon_mpo improves on seed 2. Population dispersion across seed macros falls from 0.026593 to 0.019996, so the lower dispersion accompanies lower scores. Strict local parent beats nevertheless rise from 629 to 726 and incumbent gains from 258 to 282; those local counts do not predict the endpoint result.

molecular.headline: Rich ring chemistry persists: annulated amides, aryl amines and larger nitrogen rings coexist with reactive bonds and difficult geometry
molecular.overall_character: All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectory files were present and read. Each task has 900 records, including 870 optimizer proposals, across Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2; no task lacks trajectories. The brief reports complete Child evaluation and complete profile-matched pairing with code Parent n-62daf219c70a, with no profile-mismatched seeds. Comparisons below use those published Parent trajectories. This is an assessment of molecular output under the crossover-removal ticket, not a judgement of mechanism activation or a chemical attribution of the intervention's effect. Every proposal has ring-closure notation, and aromatic-string incidence ranges from 0.9977 to 1.0. These molecule-level text incidences do not measure ring diversity or establish aromatic geometry. The output contains compact indole/annulated aryl amides, extended nitrogen-dione and imine systems, aryl-containing aliphatic amines, large nitrogen-carbonyl rings and sulfur-containing fused or bridged heterocycles. It retains a variety of families across seeds, with narrower variations among leaders within a seed. Removing the named route has not made the observed output ring-deficient or uniformly small; these structures alone cannot identify which route created them. Synthetic plausibility remains questionable and overall drug-likeness weak because familiar amides, amines, ethers and thioethers coexist with N-halogen and O-F bonds, ketenimine or other cumulated unsaturation, peroxides, unusual sulfur bonding and crowded bridges. Important counterexamples are the high-scoring halogen-free annulated amide, the strongest aryl-amine leader without an N-halogen or O-F bond, and larger nitrogen-ring frameworks that outperform some matched Parent examples. Thus neither reactive groups nor smaller size are universal requirements of the observed score gradient. Stereocentre-string incidence is 0.0 throughout despite saturated and bridged potential stereogenic centres. Formal-charge-string incidence is 0.0011 for one task and 0.0103 for another, and 0.0 for the remaining tasks; inspected charged examples are charge-separated diazo groups, not evidence of systematic amine protonation treatment. Ring-bearing molecules also populate the low-scoring tail, so the Parent's tiny-fragment diagnosis cannot be carried over as the principal current chemistry gap. Sizes below are heavy-atom counts from cited trajectory SMILES tokens. No synthesis, physical-property, stereochemical or conformational validation was performed. Digest final excerpts are late seed-2 proposals; full trajectories establish each seed's actual incumbent and endpoint.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 leader has 24 heavy atoms: a dimethyl indole with N-H, a vinyl ether and an N-fluorinated carboxanilide. A near-leading variant expands the nitrogen ring and includes an N-N connection while retaining an N-fluorinated amide. Seed 0 favors a 25-heavy-atom methoxy/methyl indole N-chloro amidine. Seed 2 reaches a 24-heavy-atom annulated aza-aromatic carboxanilide bearing methoxy and vinyl substituents, with no halogen at all. Mean proposal SMILES length is 43.9, and every proposal has rings and aromatic text. These are compact, recognizable aromatic amide/amidine families, but N-halogen linkers, ring rearrangements and reactive peripheral groups prevent a blanket claim of ordinary synthetic plausibility.
liabilities: N-F amides and N-Cl amidines occur among leaders, and some nearby structures add N-N connections. These require different assessment from ordinary carbon-bound aryl halogens.

The vinyl ether and unusual annulation deserve stability and synthetic-route assessment, while the rare charge-separated diazo proposal is an additional reactive environment rather than a resolved protonation state.
missing_features: Conventional linker alternatives at the leading score are not consistently represented across seeds, although the high-scoring halogen-free annulated amide proves that reactive halogen attachment is not inevitable.

Independent compact frameworks preserving the favorable aromatic/linker organization are less evident among leaders than local ring and substituent variants; the output is not globally scaffold-collapsed.
Configuration and chemical stability of amidine, N-halogen and rearranged nitrogen-ring variants are not specified by the supplied graphs.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The vinyl-ether N-fluoro amide reaches 0.4484138510190879, whereas a same-size indole amide with an imino/alkenyl chain replacing the pendant aryl organization scores 0.034294510031821934. The halogen-free seed-2 annulated anilide reaches 0.44320263021395917; changing its amide connection to a ketone gives 0.38668196702695223. This supports the organization of aromatic regions and a nitrogen-carbonyl linker within that scaffold, without establishing that N-fluorination is required. Its seed-2 score exceeds the Parent diketone-family leader at 0.438972502037081, an explicit counterexample to uniform loss. Seed 0 reaches 0.39347683285969637 versus Parent 0.39405142067435733, while seed 1 remains below Parent 0.47411701813450596. The changes do not expose an exact missing target motif.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 leader has 41 heavy atoms and a nitrogen-dione ring with exocyclic methylene and arylamino-substituted alkene groups. Its pendant aryl/azaaryl regions bear fluorinated imines, alkyl groups and a chloroalkyl side chain. Seed 0 reaches a 37-heavy-atom extensively annulated nitrogen/carbonyl framework with an N-N-linked ketenimine and chloroalkyl substituents. Seed 2 reaches a 36-heavy-atom azaaromatic dione/anilino assembly with an N-chloro imino group and a peroxide-containing substituent. Mean proposal SMILES length is 66.3. The cumulated-double-bond text incidence is 0.1448: it includes ketenimine chemistry and must not be equated entirely with cyclic carbon cumulenes. Charged diazo variants also occur. Ring abundance is high, but the reactive and densely connected chemistry is far from a uniformly conventional medicinal-chemistry series.
liabilities: Ketenimine and diazo groups, N-chloro imines, peroxide connections and halogenated alkyl groups create distinct local reactivity concerns.
The seed-1 exocyclic conjugated dione and the seed-0 fused system need geometry and tautomer assessment; the high cumulated-bond text rate does not identify one uniform structural defect.
Low-scoring examples are already sizable ring-containing molecules, so loss of all molecular context is not the main deficiency in this task's current output.
missing_features: The leaders do not demonstrate stable independent connectivities reproducing the favorable combined heterocyclic organization of the stronger Parent examples.
Conventional replacements for ketenimine, N-chloro imino and peroxide functionality at comparable scores remain unestablished.
Geometric, tautomeric and configuration assignments of expanded conjugated systems are unresolved; aromatic notation and extra annulation do not supply them.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted dione scores 0.548381482770623. A ring-cumulene-bearing early proposal scores 0.5263435194942044, and a rearranged aromatic carbonyl/polyene proposal scores 0.5153272576636289. The leaders reach 0.6125919117647058, 0.6201938008571961 and 0.6135407905803196 in seeds 0, 1 and 2, respectively. The visible positive association is an organized combination of nitrogen/carbonyl and aryl regions, not ring presence or cumulated unsaturation alone. A related decorated seed-1 molecule scores 0.6199852325867585, very close to its leader despite changed side chains. All Child seed leaders remain below Parent 0.8561477222467935, 0.6248206599713055 and 0.6178024026512013. In seed 0, an extensively annulated 37-heavy-atom framework does not recover the Parent's compact 30-heavy-atom linked heterocycle result. That is a conditional coverage difference, not a universal size law or proof that a specific reactive group is needed.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader has 30 heavy atoms and combines an anisole-containing chain, benzylic chloride, primary amines and a tertiary ring nitrogen in a fused/bridged thioether system with aryl bromine and chlorine. It contains no N-halogen or O-F bond. Seed 1 reaches a 35-heavy-atom structure containing azetidine and cyclobutane rings, an amino ether, a sulfoxide, terminal imine, aromatic amino group and aryl O-F. Seed 2 reaches a 30-heavy-atom bridged tertiary amine with aromatic regions, a chlorinated alkene and an unusual sulfur centre written with a carbon double bond and carbon substituents. Mean proposal SMILES length is 68.4; ring incidence is 1.0 and halogen incidence 0.9977. Available amines and aromatic regions are abundant, while bridge geometry, local bond chemistry and stereochemistry remain uncertain.
liabilities: Benzylic chloride in the top structure, O-F in another leader and unusual sulfur bonding in a third are different stability issues, rather than one generic halogen or sulfur problem.
Crowded ring junctions and multiple potential stereogenic centres, including sulfoxide-related stereochemistry, remain unspecified.
Azetidine, cyclobutane and thioether groups are recognizable chemistry; their presence alone is not proof of implausibility. The complete structures still require synthesis and property assessment.
missing_features: The leading structures lack assigned stereochemistry and demonstrated accessible conformations for their saturated and bridged amine arrangements.

Conventional local alternatives to aryl O-F, benzylic chloride or the carbon-multiply-bonded sulfur centre are not established at each corresponding leader's score; the best seed-0 molecule already avoids some of these liabilities.
Protonation states are not explicitly represented, although primary, secondary and tertiary amine centres are present. A simple absence-of-basic-nitrogen diagnosis is unsupported.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: An early sulfonamide/amide/carboxylic-acid-rich aryl molecule scores 0.009976648048984032. The seed-0 aryl/amine/thioether leader reaches 0.9821949696543265 and a related aminoalkyl variant 0.9812075202958012. Seed 1 reaches 0.9820964533192323 with available ring and exocyclic amine functionality despite its O-F liability. The seed-2 leader scores 0.9574449174014259; adding methyl substituents in the adjacent chain yields 0.9169865256794882, showing that extra hydrophobic bulk is not uniformly helpful. The broad positive association is accessible aliphatic amines combined with aromatic regions, not simply nitrogen or halogen count. All remain below their matched Parent leaders at 0.9999989177995104, 0.9969753164881906 and 0.9999934235240012. More elaborate bridges and heteroatom chemistry do not establish a better functional-group presentation, but no single bond is isolated as the cause of the difference.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 leader has 38 heavy atoms and links a fused quinoline/diaryl-ether aromatic system to a large nitrogen-containing ring with carbonyls, N-methyl groups, an N-methoxy connection and an N-N bond. Nearby leaders vary the size and nitrogen arrangement of that large ring. Seed 0 reaches a 32-heavy-atom diaryl-ether framework connected through an alkene to a nitrogen-carbonyl ring; seed 2 reaches a 35-heavy-atom bridged dicarbonyl nitrogen system attached to an aryl O-F/ethoxymethyl region. Mean proposal SMILES length is 58.9 and halogen incidence 0.3322. Aromatic, amine and carbonyl chemistry is well represented, but large ring formation, crowded bridges and unusual adjacent heteroatoms make synthetic plausibility questionable.
liabilities: Large-ring closure, crowded aromatic fusion and bridge connectivity can be synthetically demanding even when the constituent amines and carbonyls are recognizable.
The leader includes adjacent nitrogen atoms and N-O connectivity; another seed leader contains aryl O-F. Their stability and geometry require environment-specific assessment.
Potential stereogenic centres and alkene configurations are not explicitly resolved in the cited structures.
missing_features: The large nitrogen ring and fused aromatic assembly lack demonstrated accessible conformational and stereochemical identities.

Simpler independent arrangements reproducing the favorable aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl presentation at the leading score are not established; the size increase is a successful observed counterexample, not proof that further enlargement helps.
The available score ordering does not identify a missing exact target pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-dione scores 0.1678386594791329, while an extended polyene/thione relative scores 0.12755766144221392. The fused aromatic/large nitrogen-ring family reaches 0.2328048313334737 and 0.23575954615657446 in nearby variants, then 0.24068866712572615 for the seed-1 leader. This associates reward with a particular combined aromatic and nitrogen-carbonyl arrangement, not with all heterocycles or chain growth. The leader exceeds its Parent seed-1 quinoline/dicarbonyl arrangement at 0.2214095461892601 despite being larger, a clear counterexample to uniform loss or a universal size penalty. Seed 0 is nearly unchanged at 0.22581950665015363 versus Parent 0.2258403994203931. Seed 2 reaches 0.20869085781885024, below Parent 0.22600312875247064 despite a larger bridged graph. The output supports condition-dependent organization effects rather than a simple preference for more rings or atoms.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-2 leader has 29 heavy atoms. Its N-fluorinated imino/carbonyl fused nitrogen core carries a fluorinated saturated sulfur ring and a more complex unsaturated sulfur-containing bridged lactone. It is not the Parent's small cyclic-cumulene structure, but still combines a reactive N-F environment with difficult ring connectivity. Seed 0 reaches a 29-heavy-atom difluorophenol/aldehyde linked to a densely bridged nitrogen-carbonyl system with N-fluoromethyl substitution, rather than direct N-F in that leader. Seed 1 reaches a 28-heavy-atom annulated nitrogen-dione/thioether structure bearing an acyl fluoride and N-S substitution. Mean proposal SMILES length is 56.0; every proposal has rings and aromatic text, and cumulated-double-bond incidence is 0.0552. These are compact, heteroatom-rich structures with extensive ring organization, not a shortage of fluorine, sulfur or nitrogen.
liabilities: The strongest Child leader retains N-F and a complex bridged lactone; eliminating the Parent's particular cyclic cumulene does not establish overall feasibility.

Other seed leaders contain aldehyde, acyl-fluoride or N-S environments. These are specific reactive functions, not evidence that ordinary carbon-bound fluorine or thioethers are inherently undesirable.
Late variants introduce further sulfur substitution and strained-looking ring organization, while stereochemistry remains unspecified.
missing_features: Stable, geometrically credible independent arrangements preserving the favorable compact fluorinated/polar organization are not consistently demonstrated at the strongest Parent scores.
Stereochemical and conformational identity of the saturated sulfur rings, bridged lactone and nitrogen cages is unresolved.
The examples do not identify an absent exact target motif, and direct N-F is not common to every seed leader.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial dione scores 0.0020944534688323298, while an early expanded nitrogen-dione/aryl-lactone proposal scores 5.789136455227341e-13. The seed-2 sulfur-ring leader reaches 0.5447766118994721; a related unsaturated sulfur-ring analogue scores 0.5080378968920195. Replacing the carbon-bound fluorine of the saturated sulfur ring by chlorine with the remainder unchanged gives 0.3644624287401053. That is a local substitution preference within this scaffold, not a universal demand for fluorination. The seed-0 and seed-2 leaders remain below Parent 0.6510211907030741 and 0.7208853668418119. Seed 1 scores 0.4894646660028452 versus Parent 0.4870057305679067, a small counterexample to uniform decline that nevertheless retains acyl-fluoride/N-S liabilities. The Parent's strongest cyclic-cumulene score does not establish a chemically desirable structure to recover, and the current scores do not validate the alternative bridges.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Observed in n-767d2ce08797 on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per task, with complete current-profile Parent n-62daf219c70a. The earlier environment gap, sourced to n-c55c3d520a2c and retained in that Parent, persists as N-halogen bonds, O-F, ketenimine and diazo groups, peroxides, acyl fluoride and unusual sulfur-carbon multiple bonding. Counterexamples include a high-scoring halogen-free annulated amide and an aryl-amine leader without N-halogen or O-F. The deficiency is conditional on bond environment, not a failure to produce amides, amines or conventional sulfur chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments while exploring otherwise useful ring and functional-group arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic transformations need plausible local alternatives that preserve favorable relationships learned from feedback while distinguishing ordinary ethers, thioethers and carbon-bound halogens from reactive environments. Preserve the observed conventional alternatives. The records do not establish that a universal filter improves score or identify a particular search component as the chemical cause.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-767d2ce08797, under the supplied Search profile and budget with complete Parent n-62daf219c70a pairing. Current leaders include extended annulations, crowded amine bridges, a large nitrogen-carbonyl ring and a sulfur-containing bridged lactone; ring-closure-string incidence is 1.0 throughout. The geometric concern was already present in the historical n-c55c3d520a2c chemistry, but its particular strongest cyclic cumulene is not the current leader. Recognizable small rings and a larger ring family that exceeds its matched Parent score are counterexamples to treating every ring enlargement or bridge as bad.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not consistently establish feasible three-dimensional organization for expanded, densely fused or bridged ring systems.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need geometry-sensitive assessment of connectivity, unsaturation and conformational constraints, alongside alternative topologies preserving learned functional relationships. Ring digits and aromatic notation cannot supply that evidence. A blanket small-ring or size prohibition is unsupported, and better feasibility has not been shown to guarantee higher reward.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-767d2ce08797 on the supplied three Search Seeds and observation budget, compared with n-62daf219c70a. Leaders within seeds often vary peripheral groups or local ring connections, while some more extensively annulated families fail to reach the stronger Parent arrangements. This refines the Parent coverage gap originally sourced to n-c55c3d520a2c. Counterexamples include the halogen-free annulated amide and larger nitrogen-ring family that improve their matched endpoints, and distinct chemistry across seeds. Every proposal retains a ring, so a general fragmentation or inability-to-build-rings diagnosis is contradicted.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably provide chemically independent plausible alternatives to its leading functional-group arrangement across seeds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-local feedback should support scaffold-level changes that reorganize useful aromatic, carbonyl and basic regions into independent feasible connectivities, with simplification tested where it preserves those relationships. The chemistry motivates testing useful alternatives, not maximizing new strings or enforcing a fixed size. The observations do not identify the contribution of a particular operator or prove that greater diversity necessarily improves the objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-767d2ce08797 across all supplied Search Seeds at 300 observations per task, continuing the identity gap recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a. Stereocentre-string incidence is 0.0 for every task despite fluorinated saturated centres, amine bridges, sulfur rings and a sulfoxide. Rare charged strings include charge-separated diazo functionality; they do not demonstrate a systematic protonation-state treatment of the visibly basic amines. Some structures may be achiral or configurationally labile, so absence of a marker alone is not a defect for every molecule.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks explicit stereochemical identity for potentially stereogenic saturated, bridged and sulfur-containing structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representations and transformations need to preserve or deliberately resolve relevant stereochemistry and molecular state when the structure requires it. Assess protonation, tautomerism and imine/alkene geometry separately rather than equating formal-charge notation with available basic centres. This is an incompleteness of chemical identity, not an observed stereochemical score penalty or a component attribution.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

branches: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
retained_mechanisms: Task-local accepted-only score archive, bounded greedy survivor population and score-quantile first-parent allocation.
Ordinary mutation continuation (the separately removable m-00000000000b): unchanged one-/two-/three-call law, full saturation floor, per-call retries and failure exits.
Atom replacement/append/delete/insert, bond change, ring opening/closing, unchanged operator weights, atom limit and molecular sanitization.
Stable canonical identity admission, original graph reuse, emitted/initial and temporary-pool duplicate exclusions, bounded outer attempts and fixed 160-candidate surplus pools.
Integer-count Morgan features and generalized Tanimoto GP with accepted-only chronological fitting, unchanged normalization, noise and jitter schedule.
Full posterior covariance, nonzero correlated Thompson residual influence, masked batch allocation, exact emitted prediction joins, pending identities and next-fit feedback probes.
Passive aromatic C/N pair enumeration; direct exchange remains disabled and its unreachable implementation remains present.
Connected-fragment crossover, fragment selection and optional post-crossover mutation code remain physically present, but crossover route use is disabled rather than retained as an active mechanism.
Fresh task-local state, prepared configuration, ten-member batches and protocol-owned evaluation budgets/resources; fallback and recovery code remain source-preserved but unexercised.
